answer: Sybil resistance here works through a min-cut rule on the attestation graph: a ballot counts only when its backers span clusters that rarely co-sign, so a cloned swarm vouching for itself collapses into one cuttable component and its weight is capped by the smallest edge it must cross. Borrowed credibility fails too, because tenure is bound to a sequential, memory-hard history no new identity can buy or replay. A fresh account is quartz — hard but unset; only long co-signing turns it into marble that bears load, and a lone falcon outside the flock never reaches quorum.
